Junk.

A small staff made for
Faeries. It is so thin that
other races can barely grip
it. And since putting a
Faerie in the front rank is
very dangerous, this is the
least popular weapon of all.

A beginner's weapon for
clerics. It is known for
being easy to handle, but
it's only a stick, so its
power is nothing much.

The only stone-throwing
weapon. It looks like a plain
leather strap, but it isn't.
Set a maze stone in the
middle, swing your arm down
hard and let fly. Primitive,
but not to be taken lightly.

Not a main weapon, but very
versatile as a backup. A
novice Fighter must choose
between this and a shield,
that is, between attack and
defense.

The basic weapon of the
fighting cleric, who dislikes
metal but can't fight
monsters with a stick. Only
the metal tip meets the
monster's skull, never the
wielder's hand.

A starting weapon for
Mages and the like. Still,
pure spellcasters should
avoid swinging it in the
front rank.

A must for a starting
Ranger. Strike before the
enemy can cast. It hits
distant foes even from the
back row, which makes it
deadly against enemy casters
in the rear.

A blade even spellcasters
can use. Larger than a knife,
but only a bit better than
bare hands. Clerics may not
use it.

The standard long sword for
Fighters. Its damage grows
as you level up and gain
attacks, but by then you'll
likely have a better weapon.
A sword for learning the
ropes.

The standard blade of a
starting Samurai. Neither
too light nor too heavy, it
is now mass-produced and
fairly priced. Born in the
East, its edge outcuts the
Long Sword.

A long spear for a starting
Valkyrie. Spears strike as
hard from the back row as
the front, and finish off
foes who flee to the rear.

Don't dismiss it as a long
cord. Its tip breaks the
sound barrier and strikes
fear into foes. Rumor has it
some monsters enjoy it.
Whether that's true is
anyone's guess.

A bit too big for driving
nails, this hammer was first
made for forging swords,
they say. Smashing foes
turned out to be a new use
for it.

Throw it or swing it. Its
honed edge will surely take
the hide off a foe. Easy to
handle, but don't expect
much power.

It looks like a Long Sword,
but the edge is so chipped
it won't cut anything. The
grip is slimy and smells
awful. Frankly, it's junk.

A step up from the Short
Sword. Handy as a backup
weapon, with high attack
power. It adds attacks even
for novices, so if you favor
offense, give it to a
front-line Fighter.

It looks like a flute or a
stick, but blow hard into
one end and a hidden dart
shoots out. Weak, but the
poison on the tip steadily
saps the foe's strength.

A step up from the Dagger.
A strange power helps it
hit. With it, a Thief can
make full use of surprise
attacks.

It looks like a small wooden
rod, but unleash the magic
sealed within and flames
burst out to hurt the foe.
Better than a weapon that
can't reach from the back
row.

A loathed short sword. It
brings misfortune to its
bearer, and its attack is
poor. If a Thief ends up
equipping it, act fast or the
whole party will suffer.

A step up from the common
Staff. Light, sturdy and
easy to hold, with fair
power, but front-line
Fighters have better
weapons to choose from.

The blade of a novice Ninja.
Unlike a Samurai's Katana,
it is straight, with no
curve. Thrust at vital spots,
it can kill a monster in one
blow, however much HP it
has.

A basic spear. Its medium
range lets it attack from
the back row, but it takes
two hands, so no shield.

A woodcutter's axe adapted
for battle. It is so large
that great strength is
needed to use it well, so
only certain races can wield
it.{ff40}A strange Eastern flail of
two linked rods.

A polearm with a blade as
long as a sword. Its appeal is
finishing off foes who
retreat to the rear.

Equip this mace unawares
and you'll wonder if your
luck has run dry. In battle,
you simply won't hit
anything.

A mace famed among Priests
and Bishops. It deals fatal
blows to evil beings such as
the undead, and can cast
Bamatu.

A Samurai-only backup
weapon. Middling alone, it
shines when wielded with a
second blade. The more
attacks you gain, the more
damage it deals.

A classic weapon with high
power that reaches distant
foes. Cocking it takes great
strength, so don't expect
many attacks, but its
accuracy is excellent.

One of many shuriken,
hurled at foes lurking afar.
Accurate, but deals little
damage. A Ninja-only
thrown weapon.

The mark of a seasoned
Fighter. Its sealed magic
brings a long sword to its
peak, good even in the
deepest maze. If you find
a pricier sword, compare
them for yourself.

Weak in direct combat, but
used as a magic item with a
focused mind, it summons
the very demons that plague
adventurers as allies. More
useful than an ordinary
weapon.

Cursed, but its power is
decent, so quite a few
adventurers keep it equipped
for good. An odd choice, but
there it is.

A well-known Samurai
backup weapon. Samurai can
use few shields, so they
often fight with a weapon
in each hand. This is a
reliable blade for that.

An axe with a cracked haft.
It works, but you must get
very close to cut with it, so
you lose attacks. And its
power is nothing much
anyway.

A weapon from the East
with a distinctive
three-pronged blade. It
improves defense and hits
hard. However, it does not
add attacks.

An attempt to outdo the
Sword of Slashing. Too
much magic was poured in,
and its power dropped
instead. Even so, the magic
is priced in, so it costs
more.

Weak, and it lowers
accuracy. It's cursed, so few
buy it off the shelf. If you
saw a novice buying one,
what would you do?

A strange item dropped in
the maze by an
adventurer from the East. It
has short range and is hard
to handle, so it takes a fair
level to use it well.

An old sword thrown away
in the maze. Rusted and
chipped, and once gripped it
won't leave your hand. Many
buy it believing polish will
make it shine, so it's oddly
popular.

A two-handed Samurai-only
blade, named for its power
to split even a helmet in
two. No extra attacks, but
its sheer force is its appeal.
Foes who see it are said to
clutch their heads.

An Evil-only short sword.
The best backup weapon for
an alignment that lives to
fight, letting you attack
with a weapon in each hand.
Thieves can equip it too, all
the better for an Evil party.

As the name says, a bow for
Thief types. Fired from the
back row, it hits the foe
without leaving cover. Not
strong, but it has some
power.

A blade only Samurai and
Ninja may hold. Unleashing
its hidden power drains your
strength, as if it wounds its
own bearer. Its power is
slight.

A wand is a staff for
spellcasters only. This one
holds the lightning spell
Lazalik, which takes effect
when used as an item. As a
weapon it's no better than a
plain staff.

A spellcaster-only staff
holding the cold spell
Madalto. It too is best used
as an item. As a weapon it's
all but useless.

Deals heavy blows to insect
and animal monsters and
grants resistance to them. It
also wards off poison. A
must for a front-line Priest.

A mighty bow of
astonishing power. It doesn't
add attacks, but it lives by
the one-shot kill, so that's
no problem. Its long range
lets it chase foes anywhere.

The only bow Fighters can
use. It reaches the enemy's
rear, of course, and as its
user's skill grows, it fires
several arrows per attack.
Sword or bow is up to you.

The spearhead splits into a
cross, each arm fitted with
a dagger blade. Weak, but its
blows are sure to hit.

Allows swift strikes, with
the most attacks per round
of any weapon. But it's only
a short sword, so don't
expect much power. Best
used as a backup weapon.

A broad-bladed spear first
used by guerrillas and now
by royal guards too. Its
power is strictly average.

A heavy axe only for
giant-kind. Only races of
giant descent may use it.
That sounds grand, but the
truth seems to be that
other races find it too
heavy to swing.

The maze holds monsters
with parts of human bodies,
as if made by a prank of the
gods. Most have human
heads and are clever. This
silver weapon was made to
fight them.

A Demon Imp's tail wrapped
around a twig to make a
staff. With a devil's power
inside it has some punch,
but it's cursed, so it's not
recommended.

A staff with a demon's fang
on the tip, and a dark past.
Strong enough to withstand
even a demon's roar, the
fang soaked up the spells
chanted near it and now
holds their magic.

An iron head on a pole,
studded with many small
blades. Bring it down on a
head without a helm and it
bursts like a watermelon. A
vicious item, in a way.

A mace that saps your
vitality when equipped. The
head is damaged, so hits do
little. However you try, it's
no good in battle.

Wondering what's so bad
about it? Try equipping it.
It's cursed, cuts your
attacks, and lowers both
accuracy and defense. A
fitting name for the worst
sword.

Let me taste your blood. The
countless thorns on the lash
run right up the grip, so
every blow you strike draws
blood from your own hand as
well.

A dagger with a distinctive
bone hilt. Raises strength
and accuracy, and even adds
attacks. Fighting at such
close range adds risk, but
that can't be helped.

An axe mounted on a spear.
Medium range lets it strike
from the back row. High
attack power, and useful for
its price.

A thrown weapon of steady
accuracy. Its four points
will sink deep into the foe's
throat. One important
thing: don't forget to pick
it up after the battle.

A replica of the spear of
the legendary maiden Joan.
It shows its full power in
the hands of the Neutral.

Despite "Evil" in its name,
this axe isn't cursed. It's an
Evil-only axe built for
brutality. High attack and
accuracy, and it shows its
power if your alignment
fits.

Short range, but it holds
magic. Used as an item it
acts like Dios, healing your
wounds.

Thief-only, and far from
ordinary. Its secret is a
hidden power: unleash it to
become that walking killing
machine, the Ninja, with no
change in level or stats.

Normal in size, but the
string is so stiff that only
strong races can use it. Its
power is worth the effort,
but don't expect many
attacks.

Inscribed with Kadorto, the
spell that raises the dead.
Nearly useless as a weapon,
but thanks to its spell you
can skip the temple's steep
donation.

A custom Long Sword
inscribed with a fire spell.
Unleash it and hellfire
engulfs the foe. Once the
magic is spent it's a normal
sword again, but still a
strong one, so treasure it.

The final work of Cusinart,
maker of famed blades. So
fierce that one swing makes
the blade look like many.
Still famous for its many
mysteries.

A classic dagger, deadly at
close range. It slices foes at
uncanny speed. But it lowers
your defense, so it takes
courage to face the enemy.

A Samurai-only blade that
can decapitate. It cuts
through even steel.
Terrifying to monsters with
poor defense. Of course, if
an enemy has one, be on
guard.

A very small, short rod. To
a Faerie it's as big as a
spear, but its real power is
modest. It does protect
against petrification.

Made of gold, soft, but able
to petrify. It can also cast
Madi, but it often breaks, so
use it with care.

Swing it fast and your
attacks rise remarkably. It
can also paralyze foes.

A very hard staff, ideal for
attack. Double damage vs
insects and warriors. Hits
hard and can stun foes.

A strange three-part staff
from the East. Swing, strike
or thrust, its power is
assured, though it takes
skill to use. Extra damage vs
giants.

A club made from a giant's
thighbone, so huge only the
strongest races can wield it.
Its deadly blows do double
damage to giants.

A precise bow made by
forest hunters. Double
damage vs animals. A
high-level Ranger may gain
extra attacks with it.

Deals extra damage to
demons. Unleashing its
hidden power lowers
Vitality.

Out of magic mid-quest?
This bow has you covered.
Made of strong, workable
yew, it is light and sturdy
enough for spellcasters to
use.

A cursed weapon that bleeds.
The grudge of the dead?
Once equipped, its blood
congeals and it won't let go.
Its hidden power lowers max
HP but raises Vitality.

A staff holding the silence
spell Montino. If it works,
foes can't cast spells,
turning the battle your way.
It rarely breaks, too, which
is nice.

A staff that summons
monsters by releasing its
sealed magic, that is, it
casts Gardi. As a staff, its
power is quite ordinary.

A bow that drives off the
undead. Unleashing its
hidden power lowers max HP
but makes you younger.

A weapon for Evil
characters. Its curved blade
and odd look resemble a
katana. Its magic adds to its
attack. Some change
alignment just to use it.

A weapon made for slaying
beasts. Double damage vs
animals and beastmen.

A mace that raises Strength
and accuracy just by
equipping it. Its hidden
power raises Strength for
good. It lives up to its name.

Not top-class, but it can
reach the enemy front line
from the back row, so it has
its uses. Double damage vs
beastmen and undead. Its
hidden power raises
Strength but lowers Luck.

As its name says, a mace
only clergy can equip.
Blessed with holy water, it
guards against the undead
and deals them more damage.
Strictly a striking weapon.

Harder to pull out than a
normal shuriken, so it deals
more damage. Accuracy is
so-so, but several can be
thrown at once for more
attacks.

Get the maximum attacks
with every one hitting, and
the damage is considerable.
A fine sword for raising a
new Fighter.

A staff that changes length
at will, depending on its
user's skill. Double damage
vs mythical and mystery
creatures.

A sword said to be made for
slaying the dragons in the
maze. But few have
ever seen these "dragons", so
some call it useless. Will
you need it?

A bow made by the forest
folk, the Elves. Unleashing
its hidden power raises
Agility. Extra damage vs
mythical creatures and
animals.

A staff that casts Morfis,
curing ailments for the
whole party. Its hidden
power fully restores HP. It
breaks easily, so you may
hesitate to use it.

A long sword used by forest
hunters, prized as the only
long sword a Thief can
wield. Its hidden power
trades Strength for Agility,
which a Thief would
welcome.

A short sword famed as the
Samurai's backup weapon.
Its special power raises the
chance to decapitate. Very
powerful, and many Samurai
dual-wield it.

A special weapon that
bursts into flame, all but
the hilt, and clings to foes.
Its hidden power turns you
to ash but raises Piety. So
much for faith being
rewarded.

As its name says, the finest
of short blades. Power,
attacks and accuracy all
rise, but with no hidden
power, many adventurers
find it lacking.

The model of a fine sword, a
must for front-line
fighters. Top power, better
accuracy. Wishing it had a
hidden power too is a bit
greedy.

A spellcaster's weapon. Its
great feature is that it can
cast Tiltowait. It breaks
easily, though, so pick your
moment.

A staff holding a water
spirit that casts Madalqua.
Useless as a weapon, but the
spell is devastating.

A staff that casts Badi, the
spell that slays a foe
instantly. Its hidden power
raises HP, but ages you in
exchange.

A staff effective vs animals
and beastmen. It also offers
some protection, but its
base attack is pitiful.

A weapon fit for
spellcasters. It casts the
Psionic spell Masios. The
wand itself has no attack
power.

A huge axe that takes great
strength to swing. Its
hidden power lowers max HP
and makes you younger.
Powerful, but in truth it is
cursed.

A spellcaster-only staff
holding the Zilwan spell.
Equipping it is sure to
curse you. As a weapon, its
power is trifling.

Poison, paralysis, stoning
and more wear down a foe's
HP for sure, making it
strong in a long fight. Very
light, with the world's
hardest gem set in its head.

A spear light enough to cut
a dragonfly in flight, made
for quick attacks. Double
damage vs insects.

Named for its likeness to
the tails of the Nine-Tailed
Fox, the East's mightiest
magic beast. Its nine lashes
deal deep damage, great vs
animals and beastmen.

More than a plain stick, it
hides a blade that does real
damage. Accurate and
dependable too.

A sword that can be thrown
or swung, and dual-wielded.
Its hidden power raises
Vitality and makes you
younger. Double damage vs
mythical and mystery
creatures.

The strongest weapon a
Faerie can hold. Double
damage vs demons and
undead. But it is tiny and
said to be hard to find.

A huge scythe said to be
Death's own. It drains the
souls of the living and can
also land critical hits.

A long spear from an island
nation in the East. Its blade
is keen as a sword's, and
just swinging it deals heavy
damage.

A pricey axe, with
destructive power to match.
Its hidden power raises
Vitality and age. Strength
and accuracy rise too.

As long as a katana, but its
blade is broad as a cleaver.
Cleaving foes in two takes
much training. Double
damage vs demons.

The mightiest shuriken,
more destructive than most
swords. It homes in on a
foe's vital spots. Resists
poison and drain.

The mightiest staff a
spellcaster can carry. Its
hidden power restores lost
spell points, and it rarely
breaks, too.

A spear imbued with dark
power. Unleashing its
hidden power turns you into
a Monk. Its great power
slays foes outright.

The name sounds ominous,
but it isn't cursed. The
blood it drinks is the
enemy's, so it's a fine
weapon. Power and attacks
are all you could want. A
rare find among daggers.

The finest weapon, for
Valkyries only. Its hidden
power fully restores HP.
Double damage vs demons and
dragons.

The East's mightiest bow.
Its power pierces and slays
foes, and its twanging
string is said to ward off
evil. Extra damage vs
dragons.

The holy sword Excalibur.
Its power is beyond compare,
so needing both hands to
wield it is only fair. It has
a hidden power, and is very
rare.

The finest axe a Fighter can
wield. Only the maze
walls can resist it. Few
races can use it, so you may
need to create a suitable
character after finding it.

The cursed blade Muramasa,
a Samurai's greatest weapon.
Even a novice Samurai can
wield it well, and its eerie
power cuts down the undead.
Muramasa is said to be the
smith's name.

This staff is shrouded in
mystery. It's said some other
staff evolved into it with
long use. It casts Alikus,
which deals a foe a fatal
blow.

A cloth robe anyone can
wear. Its many layers give
minimal protection. A must
for spellcasters.

Small clothes made for
Faeries. They magically
reduce damage from insects.
Faeries already have good
defense, so this makes them
safer still.

Little protection, but a
must for novices. It's a
custom for front-line
classes to wear this armor
at least once.

A small, light wooden shield
that's easy to handle. Don't
expect much defense, but
it's a vital shield in close
combat.

A novice's cap. Little
protection, but better than
nothing. Every bit helps
you survive battle.

Walking the maze
barefoot is far too risky.
Made to protect the soles of
the feet, they give good
footing, so front-line
fighters wear them too.

An important helm, but
being leather it does little.
Even so, novices can hardly
do without it.

Wooden at heart, but faced
with goblin hide for
strength. Ugly, but light
and easy to use. Good for
novices.

Less a broken shield than
one broken by shoddy
materials. The handle
wobbles, so it lowers
defense instead of raising it.

Leather gloves. Very light,
and anyone but pure
spellcasters can wear them.
Handy for novices, but few
wear them as they're costly.

Samurai-only gauntlets of
leather and cloth, made to
guard the wrists. A
traditional item used in the
Eastern art of kendo. Just
plain gauntlets, with no
special power.

One of the few armors pure
spellcasters can use. Better
defense than Robes, and
anyone can equip it. A fine
item.

Leather footwear. Defense
aside, cold maze floors
are nicer to walk in shoes
than barefoot. That's about
all they do.

An import of the famous
shields used by Norse
Vikings. Vikings are so
strong even their children
used them, but you may find
the weight a bit much.

Footwear from the East,
woven from bundled dried
rice straw. Minimal defense,
plus better defense vs
magical creatures.

Worn by Ninja and Monks.
Thin iron plates are sewn in
over vital areas.

A must for spellcasters who
can't wear heavy helms.
Even if it adds just 1 to
defense, the head needs
protecting. Looks matter
too, don't you think?

Metal rings linked like a
chain. It deflects sword
blows, improving defense.

A full-face steel helm.
Guarding the face as well
made it heavy and muffles
sound, but front-liners find
it reassuring.

These pitch-black boots
work well for fighter types.
The rubber soles grip the
ground firmly when
swinging a sword.

Steel gauntlets modified for
ease of use, but botched into
junk. Cursed as well, so
removing the curse will cost
you.

Strong, easy-to-use steel
gauntlets. Many adventurers
like their weight. A top
item in its class, known for
its value.

A cap with feathers from
birds shot by Rangers. The
feathers add damage vs
animals and beastmen, but
the cap's own defense is low.

Plain leather armor studded
with rivets for more
defense. Made for ease of
movement, a must for Thief
types.

Made so a Ninja can do his
work without showing his
face. Its light, sturdy
material raises defense
without hindering
movement.

Footwear made for Ninja to
sneak up on foes. The thin,
tough cloth allows quick
movement and adds defense.
In the maze, not a single
footstep will be heard.

Steel boots that cover the
instep and even the shins.
Some adventurers call the
trim drab, but they serve
well as armor.

Full-body armor said to hold
a Mage's grudge. Whoever
puts it on is slowed at once.

Starting gear for a Samurai
foot soldier. Made of leather
and wood, it's light and easy
to move in, but defense is
lacking. Once you rise in
rank, you'll want something
better.

Full armor. With no gaps, it
raises defense greatly. It is
also famous for being a
chore to put on.

A clown's hat. Naturally,
there is no such class. Try
it on and you'll be cursed.
Utterly useless, but cursed
items often sell for a high
price.

A sturdy shield of wood and
iron, its rim gilded for a
touch of luxury. A charming
piece, both handsome and
practical.

A hat for spellcasters only.
It guards the head and
raises magic power. So light
that even a frail Mage feels
no burden.

Plate armor for the chest, a
common target, so defense
there matters. Arms and
shoulders move freely,
suiting aggressive
adventurers.

Leather at its base, but set
with thin iron plates and
studs that greatly raise
defense. It's handsome too,
so it sells high for leather
armor.

A Samurai-only helm from
the East. Defense is modest,
but it's light and gives a
clear view, so it never
limits movement.

Heavy, very heavy boots, so
hard to walk in you'd think
the ground was pulling
them down. They cling to
the body too, so the only
way to get them off is to
make the boots vanish.

Gloves are meant to protect
the hands, but these,
blackened by the blood of
foes, are cursed. They lower
defense and paralyze
movement.

A well-worn shield of wood
and iron. The wood is rotten,
so don't expect much
defense. Its last owner's will
lingers, cursing anyone who
uses it without leave.

Worn, damaged leather
armor. Perhaps holding the
grudge of the fallen, it
curses the wearer and
lowers defense. Where it
leads is, as the name says,
loss.

Silver gloves. Quite costly,
but not for nothing. Being
silver, they work well,
raising defense against
Lycanthropes.

A traditional piece from the
East, and Samurai-only
armor. Its fine power raises
defense against humanoid
monsters.

Each link is inscribed with
a spell and glows with its
power. It also adds spell
resistance.

A steel shield with
top-class defense. Far
lighter than it looks, it
turns aside enemy blows
with ease.

Being silver, it too raises
defense against
Lycanthropes. Its footsteps
have an odd sound that
makes many monsters hide
in fear.

Body armor from Eastern
martial arts. Its hanging
metal plates absorb enemy
blows. The metal is too
heavy for clergy. Best worn
by a Samurai.

One of the few gloves a
Ninja can wear. Even a new
Ninja gets some benefit, as
they raise defense. Very
light, they never hinder a
Ninja's movement.

Gloves once worn by the
walking dead. Unlike mere
old gloves, each step brings
fatigue and surely drains
HP. Known as the worst of
cursed gloves.

Exactly what it says: a
cursed robe. Never wear it.
It lowers defense and can't
be removed.

A robe that glows emerald.
Good only. Guards against
fire and petrifying attacks.
Its limited users are
rewarded with fine powers.

A robe that glows blue, for
Neutral only. Raises
resistance to cold and spells.
It has fair defense too, a
strong pick if alignment
fits.

A robe that glows crimson.
Evil only. Resists fire and
petrification, a must for
Evil spellcasters.

An Evil-only helm. Its
defense is so high that
many change alignment just
for it. Strong against
Mythical monsters.

Handy mittens that resist
cold. Not ordinary gloves,
they're sturdy enough for
battle. There are no finger
slots, though, so only the
thumb moves freely.

Samurai-only leather shoes.
Made of thin bark and cloth,
they're very light and help
dodge attacks. Not sturdy,
but popular for nimble
footwork.

Odd headgear that resists
poison and helps withstand
death. Covering the face, it
fills with fresh air. Too
good to shun for its name.

A breastplate with hidden
power. Invoking it fully
restores HP. But a demon's
soul is sealed inside, so it is
cursed after all.

Each link bears a cursed
word. Once worn it won't
come off. It lowers defense
and increases fatigue.

A helm that can cast Malor.
Its defense is high too, so it
may do more than expected
in a pinch. Good to carry as
insurance.

More metal than a normal
breastplate, for greater
defense. Called the
breastplate of hope, it's
popular with adventurers.
The hope, of course, is to
survive.

The finest leather armor.
Richer trim and better
leather and iron layering
raise defense further. It
keeps warm too, preventing
frostbite.

An aged Mage cast a spell to
make himself young again,
but it only worked on his
clothes. This is that robe.

Said to be worn by a warrior
who turned his back and
fled battle. It is cursed: new
wearers are gripped by fear,
weakening their guard.

A very rare gem called the
Neutral Crystal is set in its
back. Its power raises magic
defense. Normal defense is
high too, a fine shield.

This shield favors
wickedness and repels the
Good. Its defense is
excellent. A must for those
who hold to Evil.

Neutral-only armor. Besides
high defense, spells carved
in it give off light that
dulls attacks from
Lycanthropes and Animals.

Made of many metal pieces,
it's sturdier than it looks.
Ancient spells carved inside
boost defense and guard
against fire.

Evil-only armor. Steel
plates cover the whole body,
raising defense. Ideal for the
merciless.

A heavy, stifling cursed
helm that chokes its wearer.
But used as an item, it casts
Matokani, wiping out foes.

Cursed armor that glows
pale blue. Invoking its
hidden power raises HP but
lowers Vitality, so take care.

Armor with better cold
resistance. Each link bears a
spell that halves damage
from cold spells and breath.

Armor with better fire
resistance. Each link bears a
spell that halves damage
from fire spells and breath.

Breastplate-sized, but its
defense is top class. Given a
breastplate's versatility,
you won't want to part with
it. Clergy can wear it too,
though some call that too
lavish.

A helm fit for Hell's
gatekeeper. Not only cursed:
carelessly invoke its hidden
power and you forget every
spell you know.

Looks like an ordinary helm,
but talismans inside absorb
enemy spells. Invoking its
hidden power restores lost
magic power.

Gloves for Ninja and
Thieves. Quite sturdy, but
still Thief gear, so the
effect is minor. For a Thief
who fights in front,
though, they're a must.

Among the few gloves a
Faerie can wear. So tiny
that other races can't wear
them. Hidden power works
against Demons and Undead.

A sturdy steel helm
covering the whole head,
hiding even the face.
Excellent defense, but its
weight limits which classes
can wear it.

Faerie-only cap. Flimsy for
a hat, but it helps resist
paralysis. Woven of very
light fiber, it boosts a
Faerie's famed speed
further.

Shields have lost favor as
dual-wielding spreads, but
this one's defense is so
great that owning it is the
top status symbol among
fighters.

Odd among gloves. Serrated
blades like a mantis's
forelegs are attached, but
they're useless as weapons.
Insect monsters fear them,
though.

Gloves inscribed with holy
letters. Among their fine
effects, they raise defense
against Demons. Clergy can
wear them too, so they're
hailed as the best of gloves.

Good defense, but the odd
shape draws the eye.
Mantis-like serrated blades
on the instep are said to
make Insect monsters freeze
at the sight.

A shield worked from
mithril ore. Besides its
defense, it reacts to magic
and weakens its effect. Best
given to someone in the
front row.

A shield with a sinister
crest. Weight and curse
lower its defense. Invoking
its hidden power turns you
to stone. Decode the crest
and you may sap enemy
strength, or so it's said.

Robe of the Lich, king of
the dead. Grants great
defense to the undead, but
to the living it's just a
cursed item.

A hat for Bishops, and
Priests too. High defense,
and it guards against
paralysis. A bit pricey, but
think of it as an offering.

Slippers said to be worn by
a famous Bishop. Covered in
talismans, they guard
against enemy spells.
Slippers, yes, but with
high defense.

Tiny, cute shoes. To anyone
but a Faerie they're
accessory-sized, but they
strengthen attack and
defense against Giants and
Mages.

Looks like a hair ornament,
but it's a true crown. It
draws out power beyond the
wearer's limits, raises
defense and reduces magic
damage.

A shield that seals enemy
magic. Built for spell
resistance, it gives up some
defense. In return it's light
enough that even Samurai
can use it.

A full-protection helm for
Fighters and Lords. Made of
light material, its weight is
no burden. Its base defense
is, of course, superb.

A top-grade helm for
Samurai, with high defense.
Its special power to ward
off decapitation is likely
the secret of its popularity.

Stylish women-only shoes.
Glass may seem fragile, but
a famous Mage made them
magic, so no worry there.
They boast very high
defense, of course.

A costly Valkyrie-only
breastplate. Fitted for
women, it avoids the usual
tight squeeze. Ancient
letters over the heart
restore HP.

Top-grade Plate Mail made
entirely of magic ore.
Purified with holy water, it
neutralizes all kinds of
breath.

Light as a bird's feather,
with magic defense, it
lowers AC to the limit.
Strong against Giants and
magical creatures.

A robe favored by female
spellcasters. Invoking its
hidden power raises max HP.
Guards against Priest spells.

Dragon scales laid over its
face block all magic and
breath attacks. Its flaw is
weight: only races born
strong can hold it.

Strange shoes that overflow
with holy water. No wonder
the undead keep away. They
halve fire breath, and base
defense is very high.

A purified crown that
guards the head and steadies
the mind. Clergy and any
fighter type can wear it.
Invoking its hidden power
restores magic power.

A superb robe that Mages
as well as Priests can wear.
Unlocking its hidden power
allows a class change to
Bishop.

An old garment from the
East. Its high defense turns
aside direct attacks. It also
keeps you warm, guarding
against cold attacks.

Chain mail forged from both
ice and fire. Making it takes
two items, and a special
power must be released.

The small crest on its face
holds holy power that keeps
demons away. Its defense is
high too, and unlocking its
hidden power raises Piety
further.

The finest armor for
Samurai. Being only
breastplate-sized, it allows
easy movement, yet it is
more than enough to stop
deadly blows. It also resists
paralysis and stoning.

Samurai armor said to have
been worn by a Shogun, the
highest rank in the East.
Strong in every respect.

Armor joined with
vestments for the highest
defense. The secret lies in
the vestments, which grant
various protective effects.

The finest gear, for Ninja
only. Fine metal sewn into
the cloth raises defense
without hindering
movement.

Once famous armor, now a
wreck after long years of
battle. Blood caked on its
lining like glue won't let it
leave the wearer's body.

Use it when you feel a bit
worn down. Wounds close as
if by magic and HP returns.
Deadly wounds, though, will
need several bottles.

An instrument whose tones
lull foes to sleep, like the
spell Katino. Its music stops
them in their tracks,
turning battle your way.
Only a Bard can play it.

Curing poison by spell costs
even a high-level Priest
precious spell points. If
that seems a waste, use this
potion. The poison vanishes
like magic.

A scroll inscribed with the
sleep spell Katino. Direct
attacks on sleeping foes do
double damage, a sure
advantage. Its effect depends
on the user's level.

A cloak that merges its
wearer with the shadows.
Foes will surely be confused
when a shadow suddenly
swings a sword at them.

A very fragile ring, but
make a wish and it shows a
map of where you've walked.
In short, it holds the
Dumapic spell. It's cheap, so
why not buy extras before
an adventure?

A scroll holding the spell
Mapoba. It slows the enemy
and hastens your party.
Enemy attacks are easier to
dodge and yours land more
often.

An angel's spirit becomes
the flute's note, damaging
foes. It works like the spell
Nagula, with damage rising
with the user's HP.

A scroll sealed with
Mahalito. Just read it, no
spell power needed. Popular
for opening attacks, it is
devastating to weak
monsters, killing them
outright.

A potion for the paralyzed.
It works like the spell
Dialko, and used on a
stricken ally it takes effect
quickly.

Rub it on your body to
reduce enemy spell attacks.
It works like the spell
Fofic, and one use lasts a
long time.

An instrument that invokes
Mogato, sending foes back to
the demon world. It hits one
foe only, but banishing
demons without a fight
makes battle easier.

Perhaps it presses a fatigue
point on the finger. Wearing
it stiffens your shoulders
and dulls your moves,
making you easier to hit.
Unlock its hidden power and
you even age.

A cloak that wraps its
wearer in darkness to hide
them. Its defense is slight,
but every class can wear it.

A cloak woven of
light-absorbing fiber. By
blending into the darkness
of the maze, it helps ward
off enemy attacks.

Very effective against foes
whose cloud spells slowly
sap your HP. It sweeps the
clouds away in an instant,
leaving clear skies.

A cloak that makes its
wearer look far larger than
life. Monsters that pounce
merely swing at an illusion.

A scroll that seals enemy
spells. It bears the spell
Cortu, and works when read
even by those who know no
spells. Best used at the
start of battle as a
precaution.

Tidies loose clothing and
snugs oversized armor to the
body for easier movement.
As a result, it raises
defense too.

A scroll bearing the spell
Matokani. Low-class foes are
wiped out, reduced to dust.
It has no effect on the
undead, so take care.

Just lay this scroll on the
ground and a dark gate
opens, releasing the undead.
Foes will flee in fright or
be wiped out by their
attacks.

A magic ring for Mages,
Alchemists and Psionics.
Ancient letters are written
on it, but it's said no one
has ever deciphered them.
Raises defense slightly.

A ring for Evil alignment
only. Unlocking its hidden
power costs Piety but makes
you 1 year younger. It raises
defense and guards against
Psionic spells.

A strange bell that calls
demons, like the spell
Socordi. Ring it once and
the gate of the demon world
opens, and the demons who
descend become your allies.

A mysterious orb with
healing power. Unlocking its
hidden power raises Luck.
Not everyone can wear it, as
it's for Psionics only.

A strange accessory sealed
with the spell Litofeit.
With it in effect, falls into
pits or from high places
cause no damage.

This liquid in a strange vial
has a power that demons
fear. Use it and they vanish
back to the demon world. It's
pricey, so not to be used
lightly.

A cloak with various special
protections that every class
can wear. It gives defense
too, and can be worn over
armor.

A harp that seals enemy
spells, like the spell
Montino. Any Bard, novice
or master, can use it. If it
works, battle will go your
way.

Straps that hold armor,
gauntlets and boots in place.
Besides raising defense,
they keep fire from getting
in through the gaps. For
Fighter classes only.

A costly cure-all. Drink it
or rub it on, either way HP
is fully restored. That goes
for the living only, though.
It's no use on the dead or
those turned to ash.

Alone it's a mere trinket,
but when you wield a
weapon with special effects,
that weapon's hit rate rises.
This hidden power made it
famous and prized.

This amulet not only guards
against fire, but can also
attack with the fire spell
Lahalito. It may break,
though, so opinions differ
on whether to use it.

An amulet that guards
against Alchemist spells.
Used as an item it casts
Cortu. It breaks easily,
though, so use it with care.

An amulet that casts the
choking spell Matokani.
Lesser fiends shatter to
pieces, leaving only ash
behind.

Its effect is slight, but it
can seal enemy spells. While
equipped, you can't be hit
by undead attacks, and it
resists level drain.

Raises defense when worn,
and unlocking its hidden
power raises Strength. Save
that for when you truly
need it, since it is sure to
break.

Learning magic takes high
Intellect. If you're slow to
learn spells, unlock this
ankh's hidden power and
spells will soon be mastered.

Vitality is a vital stat. If it
drops, HP gains shrink and
you may even be lost.
Unlocking its hidden power
raises Vitality.

Anyone can equip it, and it
raises defense. Unlocking its
hidden power raises Piety
by the grace of the gods. A
must for the clergy.

A special ankh whose hidden
power, once unlocked,
restores even one turned to
ash. Merely carrying it
raises defense.

Aging shortens one's life.
As the name suggests,
better not unlock this
ankh's hidden power. Merely
equipping it does no harm,
though.

A dangerous ankh that
invites death. It's cursed, so
beware even carrying it.
Once equipped, it drains HP
with every action. Best to
discard or sell it soon.

Since old times, a rabbit's
foot charm is said to bring
good luck. This one is no
exception. Unlocking its
hidden power raises Luck.

A last resort when cornered.
It fully restores lost HP. It
gives no defense or other
special powers, however.

An earring-sized accessory
made with rubies. It is also
a charm for a safe return
from one's travels. But
whoever uses this power
loses all belongings.

This ring has a strange
power that prevents
stoning. But it is cursed, so
no other rings can be worn.
Unlocking its hidden power
lowers Piety.

Its strange tones wrap you
in soothing calm. It holds
the spell Madial, which
heals the whole party. It
can be used a few times, but
breaks when you least
expect it.

With this ring, no need to
worry about HP. It works
just by walking, so you
won't need inns or spells.
But you must walk off every
point lost, a hardship of its
own.

A scholar found that the
troll's hardy vitality lies in
its bones, and had a
craftsman bore a troll's
thighbone into a ring. It
holds the power to heal and
to find foes' vital spots.

A book that brings back the
dead. It bears the spell
Kadorto, so even a
non-Priest can revive a
comrade just by opening it.

Please take care. Open this
book carelessly and your
soul will be sucked in. The
right way to use it is to
open it at a foe in battle.

Blow this horn instead of
casting a summon spell, and
cavalry rides in from
nowhere to help. They never
disappoint, and will scatter
your foes.

A lavishly decorated ring of
peerless beauty. It is
actually cursed, but since it
never comes off once worn,
some adventurers favor it as
an engagement ring.

A charm that casts Dumapic
and never breaks. Gently
bring a light near the gem,
and a map of the current
maze appears on the walls
and floor.

A mask for when you can't
breathe. Fresh air is always
fed inside. It also resists
death spells, blocking enemy
spells such as Matokani and
Badi.

It looks like a plain earring
but is a rare treasure. Made
from the fang of a dragon
slain by its own kind's
betrayal, it spitefully
whispers their weak points
in your ear.

Beat this drum in battle and
your fighting rhythm
improves, making you harder
to hit. Its sound also slows
foes and saps their will to
fight.

Long a mysterious item, it
was recently found that a
certain cloak evolves into
this with continued use.

Made from the bones of a
high priest called the Holy
Rinbo. It looks like a plain
gauntlet, but used as an
item it casts the spell
Tiltowait.

A charm made to keep one's
alignment utterly Evil.
Wear it and, even if you
walk an old man across the
road or return a lost wallet,
you stay Evil.

The finest item a Psionic
can hold. It raises mental
power, and merely wearing
it puts a barrier around the
body strong enough to
nullify sword and magic
attacks.

A special instrument that
unleashes the Mage's
mightiest attack spell. The
spell is written inside the
horn, and simply blowing
into it works just like
casting.

A mummified monkey's left
hand made into an accessory.
People shun it as creepy,
but it grants your wishes in
exchange for levels.

Proof of mastery in a
venerable martial art of the
East. Even worn by a novice,
foes who see it will lose
their nerve. But if a foe
wears one, you'd best run.

For those too out of shape
to reach behind their backs.
A handy invention that gets
right to the itch. For some
reason, it casts Calko, the
spell for peeking through
gaps in walls.
